title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation, North Charleston SC
description: 787 suppliers in the Lowcountry: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit files prepared and reviewed for your Responsible Level 3. Tell us your audit date.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap Audit Documentation for North Charleston's 787 Supply Base
html:
Composite fabricators, machine shops, interiors makers and repair contractors in the Charleston area who supply the 787 program or defense aviation will find this page useful in the weeks before a Nadcap assessor or a prime's supplier quality team arrives. Atlantis NDT brings ASNT NDT Level III consulting to that job: we put together and check the audit documentation for NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114, and your Responsible Level 3 approves it. Send us your audit date and scope and we reply within one business day.

Our role in the program, and the decisions we leave to your company

Every NAS 410 program answers to a single individual. The employer appoints a Responsible Level 3 in writing, and that individual carries the authority to approve the written practice, the training courses and instructors, the examinations and examiners, and any outside agency the company uses. Atlantis is never that person for a client. We do not certify personnel to NAS 410, we offer no NAS 410 training, and we give no NAS 410 examinations. The certifications on your inspectors' files are issued by your company, under your written practice, on the strength of your records.

Our part is preparation and review. A Level III from Atlantis compares what you have on paper with three yardsticks: the Revision 6 text of NAS 410, the Nadcap assessor's AC7114 checklists, and whatever your customers flow down through their purchase orders. Then we draft what is missing for your Responsible Level 3 to consider, sort out personnel files, rehearse the audit with you and help gather evidence for any corrective actions. If your Responsible Level 3 rejects or rewrites a draft, that is the program working as NAS 410 intends.

The full service, without the local detail, is described under NAS 410 audit compliance documentation. How the standard is built and why the employer certifies is explained in NAS 410 explained.

A 787 campus that keeps growing

Boeing chose North Charleston in 2009 for 787 final assembly and delivery, and the site now runs the full Dreamliner production cycle, fabricating, assembling and delivering the 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10. Boeing said in November 2025 that Boeing South Carolina employs more than 8,200 people across its North Charleston and Orangeburg campuses. The same announcement broke ground on a site expansion: a second final assembly building similar in size to the existing one of roughly 1.2 million square feet, a parts preparation facility, a vertical fin paint facility, more flight-line stalls at the airport campus and additions to the Interiors Responsibility Center, where many 787 interior components are made. Boeing tied the program to a production rate of ten airplanes a month in 2026 and more than 1,000 new jobs over five years.

Growth on that scale pulls suppliers toward the Lowcountry. The South Carolina Department of Commerce counts more than 500 aerospace and aviation companies in the state and reports that Eaton is expanding aerospace manufacturing in Charleston County. Upstate, Woodward is building a new manufacturing site in Spartanburg County. The state's logo wall of aerospace employers includes Lockheed Martin, GE Aerospace, Safran, GKN Aerospace and Honeywell. The joint military base in North Charleston and Naval Weapons Station Charleston add government and defense contracting to the mix.

For NDT, rising rates mean more parts through each inspection cell, more inspectors on the roster and less slack for paperwork. Audit findings in fast-growing shops rarely concern a bad call on a part. They concern a file that never caught up with the person.

Lowcountry supplier types and where their files get tested

Supplier typeTypical NDTDocumentation pressure point
Composite detail and assembly fabricatorPulse-echo and through-transmission ultrasonics, often on automated scanners; visual and tap inspectionEach scanning technique and system defined in the written practice and on the certification
Metallic fittings and machined detailsFluorescent penetrant, magnetic particle on steel parts, eddy current at fastener holesProcess-control logs, reference standard certificates, technique approvals by part family
Interiors and secondary structureVisual inspection, occasional ultrasonics on bonded panelsWhether NDT is called out at all, and who on staff is certified when it is
Defense and maintenance contractorsEddy current, penetrant and ultrasonics to customer manualsWhich standard governs: NAS 410 by contract, a military requirement or a repair station program

The table shows why a single template written practice rarely fits. A composite shop and a fittings shop down the road can both owe NAS 410 compliance and still need very different documents.

Composite ultrasonics and the technique problem

Carbon-fiber laminates are inspected mostly by ultrasonics, and the composite side of the 787 supply chain is where technique definition matters most. Automated through-transmission and pulse-echo systems, hand-held phased array for repairs and rework, and bond-line checks on assemblies can each be a separate technique in the eyes of a customer. An auditor will ask whether the written practice lists each one, whether inspectors were trained and examined in the technique they perform, and whether the reference standards with built-in inserts or flat-bottom holes are traceable and current.

Technique sheets need the same attention. Each should name the system, transducer, couplant or water path, gain reference, scan increment, the reference standard and the accept or reject criteria from the customer document. The Level 3 approval needs to be visible on each sheet. We draft and review those sheets for Responsible Level 3 approval, following the approach on our aerospace UT procedure development page. For background on how methods compare on laminates and bonded structure, see the aerospace composite inspection guide. Calibration and reference-standard records follow the pattern in AC7114 equipment calibration records.

Ramp-up pressure: trainees, Level 1 Limited operators and experience logs

A rate increase brings new hires, and new hires bring the records Nadcap auditors sample first. NAS 410 lets trainees work under direct observation of a certified Level 2 or Level 3 while they build training and experience, and it recognizes a Level 1 Limited category for narrowly defined operations, such as running one automated scan on one product. Both are useful in a ramp-up. Both are also easy to document badly.

For trainees, the auditor wants experience logged as it is earned, with dates, the method, the work done and the signature of the certified person supervising. A single entry that says the hours were met, written on certification day, does not demonstrate anything. For Level 1 Limited operators, the scope has to appear on the certification and in the work instruction, and the operator should not be found doing tasks outside it. We review hiring-era files for these gaps and draft log formats your supervisors can keep current. The experience logs page explains what a defensible log contains, and expired technician certifications covers the tracking side once the roster grows.

Metallic fittings and fasteners: the other half of the inspection load

Not every Lowcountry supplier works in carbon fiber. Titanium and aluminum fittings, steel brackets, landing-gear-adjacent hardware and fastener holes keep penetrant, magnetic particle and eddy current inspectors busy, and those methods bring a different set of records. A penetrant line needs a daily trail: the known-defect panel comparison, black-light intensity at the inspection surface, ambient light in the booth, and checks on penetrant, emulsifier and developer. A magnetic particle bench needs field-strength verification, suspension concentration and a record that the inspector was certified for the technique and current direction in use. Eddy current inspection of fastener holes depends on reference standards whose notch sizes and certificates match the technique sheet.

Shops that run both composite and metallic work often keep the composite records in good order and let the older lines drift, because the composite work gets more customer attention. An assessor sampling the penetrant slash sheet does not care which product line earns the most. We review both sides with the same checklist, so a quiet bench does not produce the finding that holds up your accreditation. Local method pages for penetrant testing in Charleston and ultrasonic testing in Charleston give technicians the method background behind these records.

Customer source audits, Nadcap and the flow-down between them

A supplier to the 787 program usually meets two audit regimes. Nadcap assessors work from AC7114 and its method slash sheets, sampling personnel files and process records over a fixed number of days. The prime's supplier quality staff audit against their own process specifications and approvals, which may add requirements NAS 410 does not contain, such as technique-specific examinations or particular reference standards. Defense work can add a third layer through contract clauses.

The practical answer is a flow-down matrix: one table that lists each NDT requirement in each customer document and shows where your written practice meets it. When a new purchase order arrives with a different specification revision, the matrix shows at once what needs to change. We build that matrix as part of the gap review and keep it in your format. For the written practice itself, see written practice for aerospace and the record-by-record guide at aerospace NDT written practice. If you use outside labs for overflow work, their qualification evidence belongs in the same file set, as covered under subcontractor approval audits.

Revision 6 and a young inspection workforce

AIA released NAS 410 Revision 6 in December 2025 with Accuris. Besides clarifying certification requirements, it adds Appendix D, a points-based path that lets a Level 2 qualify to sit the initial Level 3 examination once enough credit has built up across designated activity categories. For a supplier base hiring heavily, the practical effect is long term: the Level 2s you certify this year could become Level 3 candidates later, but only if their activity records start now. Ask your Responsible Level 3 whether and how the written practice will adopt Appendix D, and set up the records to match.

Moving to Revision 6 is a scheduled change, not an overnight one. Your customers and your written practice govern the timing, and the standard has its own transition wording. Change the written practice, training material and examination banks in one coordinated revision so the auditor sees a consistent set. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A page helps if some of your staff came from industrial work under ASNT documents.

How we work with Charleston-area suppliers

Atlantis operates from Houston and Hyderabad. For Lowcountry clients, document review, drafting and gap reports run remotely through your secure file system. When the work needs eyes on the shop floor, one of our Level IIIs flies in to Charleston for the personnel-file audit, a walk through the inspection cells and the rehearsal audit. The on-site day is where trainee logs get compared with shift records, where technique sheets are held up against the scanner settings in use, and where inspectors answer the kind of questions an assessor asks.

Some local firms also carry maritime or industrial work with very different certification rules. We keep the aerospace program documents separate so an aerospace auditor never has to read around unrelated material. Local context is on the NDT consulting in North Charleston and NDT consulting in South Carolina pages. Suppliers with Gulfstream-related work in Georgia may also want the Savannah aerospace NDT consulting page. If you need method courses for new inspectors, Atlantis teaches SNT-TC-1A-based training, described on the aerospace NDT training in North Charleston page. Your Responsible Level 3 decides whether any outside course is credited in a NAS 410 program.

What to send us

  • Your written practice, with its revision log and the date of its last approval.
  • The Responsible Level 3 appointment letter and any agreements with outside agencies, instructors or examiners.
  • A list of customer specifications on current orders that call for NDT, with revision letters.
  • The roster of trainees, Level 1 Limited operators, Level 2s and Level 3s, with certification and vision dates.
  • Complete files for one recent hire, one trainee and one Level 2.
  • Technique sheets and reference-standard certificates for your highest-volume parts.
  • Findings and responses from your last Nadcap or customer audit.

Lowcountry audit-readiness checklist

  1. Every ultrasonic technique in use, manual or automated, is defined in the written practice.
  2. Each certification lists the techniques and any Level 1 Limited scope in plain words.
  3. Trainee experience logs are dated and signed entry by entry.
  4. Reference standards carry serial numbers and current certificates that match the technique sheets.
  5. The flow-down matrix covers every specification on active purchase orders.
  6. Vision records, including color perception, are inside the interval set by the written practice.
  7. Examination papers and practical checklists are retained with the grading.
  8. Corrective actions from the last audit have closed, traceable evidence.

faq.q: Will Atlantis serve as our Responsible Level 3 while we hire one?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not take the Responsible Level 3 role, even on an interim basis. Your company names that person in writing; NAS 410 allows either a staff member or a contracted outside Level 3. Our drafts wait for your Responsible Level 3 to approve them.

faq.q: Can Atlantis certify our new composite inspectors to NAS 410?
faq.a: No. The employer certifies its personnel under its written practice. Atlantis gives no NAS 410 training or examinations. We check that training, experience, vision and examination records support the certification your company issues.

faq.q: Is automated through-transmission ultrasonics a separate technique for certification?
faq.a: It often is, depending on your written practice and customer requirements. If a customer document treats it separately, the written practice and the certifications should too. We map that during the gap review.

faq.q: What is a Level 1 Limited certification and should we use it?
faq.a: NAS 410 recognizes Level 1 Limited personnel for a narrowly defined operation, such as one repetitive test on one product. It can suit automated lines, provided the scope is written on the certification and in the work instruction and is respected on the floor.

faq.q: How do we keep trainee records from becoming an audit finding?
faq.a: Log experience as it is earned: date, method, work performed and the signature of the certified supervisor. Retrospective summary entries are a common Nadcap finding. See experience logs.

faq.q: Does a customer source audit replace Nadcap for NDT?
faq.a: No. They are separate. Nadcap audits against AC7114; a prime audits against its own specifications and approvals. Many suppliers face both, so the written practice has to satisfy both. See Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness.

faq.q: When do we have to move to NAS 410 Revision 6?
faq.a: Your customers and your written practice set the timing, together with the transition wording in the standard. Plan one coordinated revision of the written practice, training material and examination banks.

faq.q: Do you work on site in North Charleston?
faq.a: Yes. A Level III comes to the Charleston area for personnel-file checks, inspection-cell walk-throughs and the rehearsal audit, while drafting runs remotely. Atlantis works from Houston and Hyderabad and has no South Carolina office.

faq.q: Can you help with corrective actions after a Nadcap audit?
faq.a: Yes. We work through the cause of each finding with your team and gather proof that the fix took hold, while your company writes and submits its own response. See aerospace NDT corrective actions.

faq.q: Does Atlantis hold Nadcap accreditation or prime approvals?
faq.a: No. Atlantis holds neither. The accreditation and approvals in your audit are your company's; our work is to help your documentation stand up to the auditor.
